> Generate a really big YAML file and see if this function will handle it. Maybe use `strings.Repeat()` to make sufficiently big items. (look in `*_test.go` files for examples)

```
func TestLongYAML(t *testing.T) {
	d := `
stuff: 1
`
	MaxLen := 5 * 1024 * 1024
	bufferLen := 4 * 1024
	//  MaxLen 5242880  len(dd) 5242880
	dd := strings.Repeat(d, 512*1024)
	r := NewDocumentDecoder(ioutil.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader([]byte(dd[:MaxLen-1]))))
	b := make([]byte, bufferLen)
	n, err := r.Read(b)
	if err != io.ErrShortBuffer{
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrShortBuffer: %d / %v", n, err)
	}
	b = make([]byte, MaxLen)
	n, err = r.Read(b)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected nil: %d / %v", n, err)
	}
	r = NewDocumentDecoder(ioutil.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader([]byte(dd))))
	b = make([]byte, MaxLen)
	n, err = r.Read(b)
	if err != bufio.ErrTooLong {
		t.Fatalf("bufio.Scanner: token too long: %d / %v", n, err)
	}
}
```

issue_context.title: NewDocumentDecoder fails with bufio.Scanner: token too long
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

When calling `NewDocumentDecoder` the token size for the buffer is the default which is NOT changable. Larger documents (which is likely when using a yaml separator) causes a `bufio.Scanner: token too long`

This was uncovered using kudo... the issue is https://github.com/kudobuilder/kudo/issues/1397

**What you expected to happen**:

1. size limitation should be documented if they exist
2. token size should be calling code managed

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Call `NewDocumentDecoder` with a doc larger than token size

**Anything else we need to know?**:

The fixing PR https://github.com/kudobuilder/kudo/pull/1400 provides more detail if needed.

Code concern is: https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/release-1.6/pkg/util/yaml/decoder.go#L94

duplicate of https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/issues/89 which I will now close

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):  1.17
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: 
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):

- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

I think 5MB is a good max size? (Since YAML is more verbose than proto, where the (IIRC) 1.5MB limit is enforced.)
